takes.prompt: Genre: dark folk video game soundtrack, eerie folklore, acoustic. BPM: 76. Key: D minor. Instrumental only, no vocals. Setting: Pine Hollow at night - lanterns glowing between black pines, fog on the ground, old tales of the Antler King told by the fire; hushed and unsettling, never scary. Arrangement: a slow, haunting nyckelharpa and low whistle melody over fingerpicked open-tuned guitar and a bowed-psaltery drone; an upright bass and a soft, steady groove of bodhran, frame drum and shaker run under the whole piece from the second bar to the end. No fade-out: the last bar is as full as the rest. Production: intimate wooden-room sound with a dark reverb.

Genre: dark folk battle video game music, Nordic folklore, driving and acoustic. BPM: 120. Key: D minor. Instrumental only, no vocals. The fight with the Antler King, an ancient forest guardian gone wrong, in a fog-filled clearing of standing stones and hanging lanterns - relentless, ominous, heroic underneath. Arrangement: a fierce hardanger fiddle and nyckelharpa melody over hard-strummed guitars and a droning hurdy-gurdy; an upright bass and a powerful, steady groove of war drums, bodhran, frame drum and stomping kick run under the whole piece from the second bar to the end. No fade-out: the last bar is as full as the rest. Production: raw, close, a wooden-hall reverb.

Genre: folk video game victory and dawn theme, acoustic and warm. BPM: 84. Key: D major. Instrumental only, no vocals. The quest's end: the Antler King is laid to rest and the first light of dawn rises over Pine Hollow, the fog lifting from the pines - relief, warmth, quiet triumph. Arrangement: a tender fiddle and tin whistle melody over fingerpicked guitar and mandolin, swelling with the whole band and a frame drum to one radiant climax, then ends on a long resolved major chord that rings out. Production: natural wooden-room sound.
